Definition: second person plural present indicative of G1510; ye are:--be, have been, belong.
BiblicalUsage: Esté is the word for 'you are' — the second-person plural of the verb to be. It is the word Jesus uses when He speaks to His disciples together: 'ye are the salt of the earth', 'ye are the light of the world'. The plural is the point: He speaks to them as a people.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that esté is a word for the church, not the individual alone: Jesus says 'you are' to His people together.
RelatedEvents: The Sermon on the Mount; The Vine and the Branches
